s0301.literal: The Prince of Wuling raised troops eastward from Chengdu; Zhiyuan together with the people of Shu submitted memorials asking that he not march. The prince thought this discouraged the army and imprisoned Zhiyuan on the ship.
s0301.idiomatic: The prince of Wuling marched east from Chengdu. Zhiyuan and the people of Shu jointly memorialized that he should not go. The prince took this as discouraging the troops and imprisoned Zhiyuan aboard his vessel.

s0302.literal: When the Wuling army was defeated, Zhiyuan followed the Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to his commandery.
s0302.idiomatic: When the Wuling army was defeated, Zhiyuan followed Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to his commandery.

s0303.literal: [23] Before long Jiangling fell; Liu Gong died; Wang Lin summoned him as recorder of the staff.
s0303.idiomatic: [23] Soon Jiangling fell. Liu Gong died, and Wang Lin summoned him as recorder of the staff.

s0304.literal: Liang's Emperor Jing enfeoffed Lin as Minister of Works; Zhiyuan was made deliberator in the works ministry and concurrently recorder.
s0304.idiomatic: Liang's Emperor Jing made Lin minister of works. Zhiyuan was made deliberator in the works ministry and concurrently recorder.

s0305.literal: Histories that record events have more than one tradition; annalistic works—[24] none match the Spring and Autumn—then the history of Lu is not the register of emperors and kings.
s0305.idiomatic: Histories that record events have more than one tradition; of annalistic works—[24] none match the Spring and Autumn—and the history of Lu is not the register of emperors and kings.

s0306.literal: Examining it: the documents of the Three August Ones are the Three Mounds; the policies of the Five Thearchs are the Five Canons—this is whence the meaning of canon arose.
s0306.idiomatic: The documents of the Three August Ones are the Three Mounds; the policies of the Five Thearchs are the Five Canons—whence the meaning of canon arose.

s0307.literal: Moreover, the Documents describes the Tang emperor as the Canon of Yao and the Yu emperor as the Canon of Shun—this again is the textual basis of the classics.
s0307.idiomatic: The Documents describes the Tang emperor as the Canon of Yao and the Yu emperor as the Canon of Shun—again the textual basis of the classics.

s0308.literal: Thus the meaning of canon has been long indeed.
s0308.idiomatic: Thus the meaning of canon is ancient indeed.

s0309.literal: As for Sima Qian's history and Ban Gu's Han, they narrate emperors and call it annals; from then on successors have followed one another in habit.
s0309.idiomatic: Sima Qian's history and Ban Gu's Han narrate emperors under the title annals; since then successors have followed one another in habit.

s0310.literal: When Chen Shou composed his work he named it Records; it surveys the Three Kingdoms and each goes its separate way.
s0310.idiomatic: Chen Shou named his work Records; it surveys the Three Kingdoms, each going its separate way.

s0311.literal: Only He Fasheng's Jin History changed imperial annals into imperial canons; since it is said to follow antiquity, in principle it is superior.
s0311.idiomatic: Only He Fasheng's Jin History changed imperial annals into imperial canons; said to follow antiquity, in principle it is superior.

s0312.literal: Therefore what is composed now is called the Liang Canon.
s0312.idiomatic: Therefore what is composed now is called the Liang Canon.

s0313.literal: Liang held the realm: from before the Zhongdatong era the domain was tranquil; after the Taqing era bandits and raiders pressed in one upon another—speaking from first to last, it was not wholly perfect. Hence this book is opened and divided into six sections.
s0313.idiomatic: Liang held the realm: before Zhongdatong the domain was tranquil; after Taqing bandits and raiders pressed in turn—taken from first to last, it was not wholly perfect. Hence this book is opened and divided into six sections.

s0314.literal: Because Liang Gaozu laid the foundation, following upon the end of Qi, tracing clan and seeking root, beginning from the Yongyuan era—what precedes the present, a certain number of scrolls, is retrospective narrative.
s0314.idiomatic: Because Liang Gaozu laid the foundation, following the end of Qi, tracing clan and root from the Yongyuan era—the preceding such-and-such scrolls are retrospective narrative.

s0315.literal: Liang Gaozu was born a commoner and grew up amid corrupt custom; he knew whether customs were sound or unsound and understood the people's truth and falsehood.
s0315.idiomatic: Liang Gaozu was born a commoner and grew up amid corrupt custom; he knew whether customs were sound or unsound and understood the people's truth and falsehood.

s0316.literal: When he came to rule the realm he enlarged this policy; within four reign-periods it was truly prosperous and rich.
s0316.idiomatic: When he came to rule he enlarged this policy; within four reign-periods the realm was truly prosperous.

s0317.literal: Now a certain number of scrolls are titled Great Peace.
s0317.idiomatic: Now such-and-such scrolls are titled Great Peace.

s0318.literal: The age is not always peaceful and the times not always well governed; not only after me did disorder still belong—now a certain number of scrolls are titled Narrative of Disorder.
s0318.idiomatic: The age is not always peaceful and times not always well governed; not only after me did disorder still belong—now such-and-such scrolls are titled Narrative of Disorder.

s0319.literal: Down to the year Liang Gaozu died in his carriage and the year Liang Taizong suffered disgrace, songs of praise and prison litigation turned west to Shanxi and not east to the eastern capital.
s0319.idiomatic: Down to the year Liang Gaozu died and Liang Taizong suffered disgrace, songs of praise and prison suits turned west to Shanxi, not east to the eastern capital.

s0320.literal: People who would not attend court and wandering scholars—in campaigns, rites, and music—turned to Emperor Wen and not to Liang Taizong.
s0320.idiomatic: Those who would not attend court and wandering scholars—in campaigns, rites, and music—turned to Emperor Wen, not Liang Taizong.

s0321.literal: To dispel disorder and return to the correct, the merit lies here; when order was settled and the work completed, the achievement had its owner.
s0321.idiomatic: To dispel disorder and return to the correct, the merit lies here; when order was settled and the work completed, the achievement had its owner.

s0322.literal: Now a certain number of scrolls are titled Emperor Wen.
s0322.idiomatic: Now such-and-such scrolls are titled Emperor Wen.

s0323.literal: As for when the four seas were exhausted and the Five Virtues rose and fell, then Emperor Jing succeeded and still abdicated to Chen—now a certain number of scrolls are titled Emperor Jing.
s0323.idiomatic: When the four seas were exhausted and the Five Virtues rose and fell, Emperor Jing succeeded and still abdicated to Chen—now such-and-such scrolls are titled Emperor Jing.

s0324.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Wang Lin set up the successor lord; though he did not accord with Heaven's mandate, yet it was his loyalty and integrity—now a certain number of scrolls are titled the Successor Lord.
s0324.idiomatic: General of agile cavalry Wang Lin set up the successor lord; though he did not accord with Heaven's mandate, it was his loyalty and integrity—now such-and-such scrolls are titled the Successor Lord.

s0325.literal: As for Liang Taizong, though a fine posthumous title was added, the title Great Treasure was not followed in the world—probably because he was constrained by the rebel Hou Jing.
s0325.idiomatic: As for Liang Taizong, though a fine posthumous title was added, the title Great Treasure was not followed in the world—probably because he was constrained by the rebel Hou Jing.

s0326.literal: The Chengsheng chronology, from connecting with Taqing onward, and divine-brush edicts and documents ought not be rashly altered; examined in the discussion at the end, there is reason in this.
s0326.idiomatic: The Chengsheng chronology, from connecting with Taqing onward, and divine-brush edicts and documents ought not be rashly altered; examined in the discussion at the end, there is reason in this.

s0327.literal: Affairs have beginning and end; people have occupation and conduct—between root and branch it is quite fitting to set forth and narrate.
s0327.idiomatic: Affairs have beginning and end; people have occupation and conduct—between root and branch it is quite fitting to narrate.

s0328.literal: Examining it: Zang Rongxu said histories without editorial judgment are like daily records—by this reasoning, full detail is truly required.
s0328.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu said histories without editorial judgment are like daily records—by this reasoning, full detail is truly required.

s0329.literal: Moreover, annalistic works that give the year sequence do so to take clarity and easy searching.
s0329.idiomatic: Annalistic works that give the year sequence do so for clarity and easy searching.

s0330.literal: As for when the Xianyun were fiercely rampant and choked our central plains—beginning with one ruler, ending with two lords—affairs overlap and words become confused.
s0330.idiomatic: When the Xianyun were fiercely rampant and choked the central plains—beginning with one ruler, ending with two lords—affairs overlap and words become confused.

s0331.literal: Now what precedes the division is called Northern Wei; after the division what the Gao clan supported is Eastern Wei and what the Yuwen clan held is Western Wei—thus they are distinguished.
s0331.idiomatic: What precedes the division is called Northern Wei; after the division what the Gao supported is Eastern Wei and what the Yuwen held is Western Wei—thus they are distinguished.

s0332.literal: Moreover, because covering and revealing differ in form and complexity and simplicity differ in text, the reductions and additions between them have general examples.
s0332.idiomatic: Because covering and revealing differ in form and complexity and simplicity differ in text, the reductions and additions between them have general examples.

s0333.literal: In Zhenming year 3 the capital fell; he then moved his residence to Jinling county in Changzhou.
s0333.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 the capital fell; he then moved his residence to Jinling county in Changzhou.

s0334.literal: In the thirteenth year of Sui Kaichuang he died at home.
s0334.idiomatic: In Kaichuang year 13 of Sui he died at home.

s0336.literal: Xu Boyang, styled Yinren, was a man of Donghai.
s0336.idiomatic: Xu Boyang, styled Yinren, was from Donghai.

s0337.literal: His grandfather Duzhi was a Liang deliberator-attendant in the Southern Xuzhou staff office.
s0337.idiomatic: His grandfather Duzhi was a Liang deliberator-attendant in the Southern Xuzhou staff office.

s0338.literal: His father Sengquan was a Liang eastern-palace communications attendant, concurrently in charge of the secretariat, and was famed for skill in calligraphy.
s0338.idiomatic: His father Sengquan was a Liang eastern-palace communications attendant, concurrently in charge of the secretariat, and was famed for calligraphy.

s0339.literal: Boyang was keen and loved learning, skilled in pleasing his parents in countenance, and in advance and retreat had measure.
s0339.idiomatic: Boyang was keen and loved learning, skilled in pleasing his parents by countenance, and measured in advance and retreat.

s0340.literal: At age fifteen he was famed for literary composition.
s0340.idiomatic: At fifteen he was famed for literary composition.

s0341.literal: He studied the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn.
s0341.idiomatic: He studied the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn.

s0342.literal: His household had historical books; what he read came to more than three thousand scrolls.
s0342.idiomatic: His household had historical books; what he read came to more than three thousand scrolls.

s0343.literal: In the examination he placed at the top; the Masters of Writing by board appointed him right ordinary attendant in the Liang Prince of Hedong's kingdom, eastern-palace scholar, and ink-bureau aide in the Prince of Linchuan's successor household.
s0343.idiomatic: In the examination he placed at the top; the masters of writing by board appointed him right ordinary attendant in the Liang prince of Hedong's kingdom, eastern-palace scholar, and ink-bureau aide in the prince of Linchuan's successor household.

s0344.literal: In the Datong era he went out as magistrate of Houguan and greatly won the people's harmony.
s0344.idiomatic: In the Datong era he went out as magistrate of Houguan and greatly won the people's harmony.

s0345.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Boyang crossed the sea south to Guangzhou and relied on Xiao Bo.
s0345.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Boyang crossed the sea south to Guangzhou and relied on Xiao Bo.

s0346.literal: When Bo was pacified he returned to court and still took his family to Wu commandery.
s0346.idiomatic: When Bo was pacified he returned to court and still took his family to Wu commandery.

s0347.literal: In Tianchen year 2 an edict ordered him to attend on the Prince of Jin'an in reading.
s0347.idiomatic: In Tianchen year 2 an edict ordered him to attend on the prince of Jin'an in reading.

s0348.literal: Soon he was made recorder of the staff in the Minister of Works Hou Andu's headquarters; Andu had long heard his name and, on meeting him, stepped down from his seat in courtesy.
s0348.idiomatic: Soon he was made recorder of the staff in minister of works Hou Andu's headquarters. Andu had long heard his name and, on meeting him, stepped down from his seat in courtesy.

s0349.literal: Sweet dew fell in the Leyou Park; an edict granted it to Andu and ordered Boyang to draft the letter of thanks; Emperor Wen read it and was struck with wonder.
s0349.idiomatic: Sweet dew fell in the Leyou Park; an edict granted it to Andu and ordered Boyang to draft the letter of thanks. Emperor Wen read it and was struck with wonder.

s0350.literal: Early in Taijian, Central Recorder Li Shuang, Recorder Zhang Zhengjian, Left People Gentleman He Che, Scholar Ruan Zhuo, Yellow Gate Gentleman Xiao Quan, Three Excellencies Gentleman Wang Youli, Recluse Ma Shu, Recorder Zu Sundeng, Comparison Bureau He Xun, Chief Clerk Liu Shan, and others were friends in a literary gathering; later Cai Ning, Liu Zhu, Chen Xuan, and Kong Fan also joined—men of the age all together.
s0350.idiomatic: Early in Taijian, central recorder Li Shuang, recorder Zhang Zhengjian, left people gentleman He Che, scholar Ruan Zhuo, yellow gate gentleman Xiao Quan, three excellencies gentleman Wang Youli, recluse Ma Shu, recorder Zu Sundeng, comparison bureau He Xun, chief clerk Liu Shan, and others were friends in a literary gathering; later Cai Ning, Liu Zhu, Chen Xuan, and Kong Fan also joined—all men of the age.

s0351.literal: At roaming feasts they composed fu and poetry and bound them into scrolls; Boyang wrote the preface for the collection, which spread widely in the world.
s0351.idiomatic: At roaming feasts they composed fu and poetry and bound them into scrolls; Boyang wrote the preface for the collection, which spread widely in the world.

s0352.literal: When the Prince of Xin'an was inspector of South Xuzhou, he was made central recorder in the Pacify-the-North Prince of Xin'an's household and concurrently separate-office aide of South Xuzhou, with concurrent acting administrator of Donghai commandery.
s0352.idiomatic: When the prince of Xin'an was inspector of South Xuzhou, he was made central recorder in the pacify-the-north prince of Xin'an's household and concurrently separate-office aide of South Xuzhou, with concurrent acting administrator of Donghai commandery.

s0353.literal: When the Prince of Poyang was inspector of Jiangzhou, Boyang once went on mission to visit him; the prince led his staff and Boyang to ascend Kuang Ridge and set a banquet. When the wine was deep he ordered brush and fu on twenty difficult rhymes; Boyang and Zu Sundeng finished first; the prince granted slaves and miscellaneous goods.
s0353.idiomatic: When the prince of Poyang was inspector of Jiangzhou, Boyang once went on mission to visit him. The prince led his staff and Boyang up Kuang Ridge and set a banquet. When the wine was deep he ordered brush and fu on twenty difficult rhymes; Boyang and Zu Sundeng finished first, and the prince granted slaves and goods.

s0354.literal: When the Prince of Xin'an returned to the capital, he was made supernumerary deliberator in the Prince of Linhai's successor household.
s0354.idiomatic: When the prince of Xin'an returned to the capital, he was made supernumerary deliberator in the prince of Linhai's successor household.

s0355.literal: In the spring of year 11 the heir apparent visited the imperial university; an edict ordered the Prince of Xin'an at the Piyong to set a Lunyu topic, and Boyang was further ordered to compose the Piyong eulogy—he received excellent reward.
s0355.idiomatic: In spring of year 11 the heir apparent visited the imperial university; an edict ordered the prince of Xin'an at the Piyong to set a Lunyu topic, and Boyang was further ordered to compose the Piyong eulogy—he received excellent reward.

s0356.literal: [25] He was made deliberator of the staff in the Pacify-the-Right Prince of Xin'an's household.
s0356.idiomatic: [25] He was made deliberator of the staff in the pacify-the-right prince of Xin'an's household.

s0357.literal: In year 13 he heard of his elder sister's death, took ill, and died—age sixty-six.
s0357.idiomatic: In year 13 he heard of his elder sister's death, took ill, and died at sixty-six.

s0359.literal: Zhang Zhengjian, styled Jianze, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
s0359.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengjian, styled Jianze, was from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

s0360.literal: His grandfather Gaizhi was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Bohai and Changle commanderies.
s0360.idiomatic: His grandfather Gaizhi was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Bohai and Changle commanderies.

s0361.literal: His father Xiuli was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; he returned to Liang and still received his former post, then was transferred to governor of Huaifang.
s0361.idiomatic: His father Xiuli was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; he returned to Liang and still received his former post, then was transferred to governor of Huaifang.

s0362.literal: Zhengjian from youth loved learning and had pure talent.
s0362.idiomatic: Zhengjian from youth loved learning and had pure talent.

s0363.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace, Zhengjian at thirteen presented a eulogy; Jianwen deeply praised it.
s0363.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace, Zhengjian at thirteen presented a eulogy; Jianwen deeply praised it.

s0364.literal: Jianwen by nature esteemed scholarship; whenever he himself ascended the seat to explain the classics, Zhengjian often attended the lecture hall, requested resolution of doubtful meanings, spoke and received in harmony, advanced and retreated with detailed elegance—all four sides fixed their eyes on him.
s0364.idiomatic: Jianwen by nature esteemed scholarship; whenever he ascended the seat to explain the classics, Zhengjian often attended the lecture hall, requested resolution of doubtful points, spoke and received in harmony, and advanced and retreated with detailed elegance—all four sides fixed their eyes on him.

s0365.literal: Early in Taqing he placed at the top in the target-shooting examination and was made left ordinary attendant in the Prince of Shaoling's Liang kingdom.
s0365.idiomatic: Early in Taqing he placed at the top in the target-shooting examination and was made left ordinary attendant in the prince of Shaoling's Liang kingdom.

s0366.literal: When Liang's Emperor Yuan took the throne, he was made direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then transferred to magistrate of Pengze.
s0366.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Yuan took the throne, he was made direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then transferred to magistrate of Pengze.

s0367.literal: As Liang's end brought turmoil, he took refuge on Kuangsu Mountain; at the time Jiao Sengdu held the masses and kept himself secure, sent envoys to request alliance—Zhengjian feared this, declined with humble words yet extended acceptance, but still held himself by ritual and law; Sengdu also by refinement mutually respected and feared him.
s0367.idiomatic: As Liang's end brought turmoil, he took refuge on Kuangsu Mountain. Jiao Sengdu then held the masses and kept himself secure and sent envoys to request alliance. Zhengjian feared this, declined with humble words yet extended acceptance, but still held himself by ritual and law; Sengdu also by refinement respected and feared him.

s0368.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, an edict summoned Zhengjian back to the capital; he was made acting aide in the ink bureau of the Pacify-the-East Prince of Poyang's household and concurrently chief clerk in the Prince of Hengyang's household.
s0368.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, an edict summoned Zhengjian back to the capital; he was made acting aide in the ink bureau of the pacify-the-east prince of Poyang's household and concurrently chief clerk in the prince of Hengyang's household.

s0369.literal: He served in succession as supernumerary recorder in the Prince of Yidu's household and compiler-historian gentleman, with concurrent acting administrator of Xunyang commandery.
s0369.idiomatic: He served in succession as supernumerary recorder in the prince of Yidu's household and compiler-historian gentleman, with concurrent acting administrator of Xunyang commandery.

s0370.literal: By cumulative promotion he became gentleman of the revenue bureau in the Masters of Writing and direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, compiler-historian as before.
s0370.idiomatic: By cumulative promotion he became gentleman of the revenue bureau in the masters of writing and direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, compiler-historian as before.

s0371.literal: He died in the Taijian era—age forty-nine.
s0371.idiomatic: He died in the Taijian era at forty-nine.

s0372.literal: He had a collection in fourteen scrolls; his five-character poetry was especially fine and circulated widely in the world.
s0372.idiomatic: He had a collection in fourteen scrolls; his five-character poetry was especially fine and circulated widely in the world.

s0373.literal: Cai Ning, styled Ziju, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
s0373.idiomatic: Cai Ning, styled Ziju, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

s0374.literal: His grandfather Zun was a Liang minister of the masters of writing and golden-glow grandee.
s0374.idiomatic: His grandfather Zun was a Liang minister of the masters of writing and golden-glow grandee.

s0375.literal: His father Yangao was a Liang attendant in the yellow gate.
s0375.idiomatic: His father Yangao was a Liang attendant in the yellow gate.

s0376.literal: Ning's rank and position were not yet high, but talent and standing were weighty in the age; he regularly sat upright in the western studio—unless they were by nature noble and famous, he rarely received them; those who curried favor often ridiculed him.
s0376.idiomatic: Ning's rank and position were not yet high, but talent and standing were weighty in the age; he regularly sat upright in the western studio—unless they were by nature noble and famous, he rarely received them; those who curried favor often ridiculed him.

s0377.literal: Emperor Gaozong once said to Ning: "I wish to use the Prince of Yixing's son-in-law Qian Su as yellow gate gentleman—what is your opinion?
s0377.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once said to Ning, "I wish to use the prince of Yixing's son-in-law Qian Su as yellow gate gentleman—what is your opinion?

s0378.literal: " Ning answered with stern countenance: "Kinsmen of the imperial district—if favor comes by imperial intent, then there is nothing further to ask.
s0378.idiomatic: " Ning answered with stern countenance, "Kinsmen of the imperial district—if favor comes by imperial intent, there is nothing further to ask.

s0379.literal: If measured by collective deliberation, for the posts of yellow gate and scattered cavalry one needs combined excellence in family and person—only Your Majesty may judge.
s0379.idiomatic: If measured by collective deliberation, for the posts of yellow gate and scattered cavalry one needs combined excellence in family and person—only Your Majesty may judge.

s0380.literal: " Emperor Gaozong fell silent and stopped.
s0380.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozong fell silent and stopped.

s0381.literal: Su heard and bore resentment; he had the Prince of Yixing daily slander him to Emperor Gaozong; soon he was removed from office and transferred to Jiaozhi.
s0381.idiomatic: Su heard and bore resentment; he had the prince of Yixing daily slander him to Emperor Gaozong; soon Ning was removed from office and transferred to Jiaozhi.

s0383.literal: When Houzhu succeeded, he was made deliberator in the Prince of Jin'an's household, then transferred to attendant in the yellow gate.
s0383.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded, he was made deliberator in the prince of Jin'an's household, then transferred to attendant in the yellow gate.

s0384.literal: Houzhu once set a drinking party; the ministers were very merry and were about to move the feast to Hongfan Palace; the crowd all followed—only Ning and Yuan Xian would not go.
s0384.idiomatic: Houzhu once set a drinking party; the ministers were very merry and were about to move the feast to Hongfan Palace; the crowd all followed—only Ning and Yuan Xian would not go.

s0386.literal: " Ning answered: "Changle's dignity is not to be passed after wine—your servant dare not accept the edict.
s0386.idiomatic: " Ning answered, "Changle's dignity is not to be passed after wine—your servant dare not accept the edict.

s0389.literal: " He at once ordered him led out.
s0389.idiomatic: " He at once ordered him led out.

s0390.literal: Another day Houzhu said to Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng: "Cai Ning relies on his standing and prides himself on talent—there is no use for him.
s0390.idiomatic: Another day Houzhu said to minister of personnel Cai Zheng, "Cai Ning relies on his standing and prides himself on talent—there is no use for him.

s0391.literal: " Soon he was transferred to chief clerk in the Trust-the-Might Prince of Jinxi's household; depressed and without achieving his aim, he sighed and said: "Heaven's Way has decline and rise; the Master said 'rejoice in Heaven and know fate'—this principle can nearly be reached.
s0391.idiomatic: " Soon he was transferred to chief clerk in the trust-the-might prince of Jinxi's household. Depressed and without achieving his aim, he sighed and said, "Heaven's Way has decline and rise; the Master said 'rejoice in Heaven and know fate'—this principle can nearly be reached.

s0392.literal: " He therefore composed the Little Chamber Fu to show his intent—very fine in reasoning and pattern.
s0392.idiomatic: " He therefore composed the Little Chamber Fu to show his intent—very fine in reasoning and pattern.

s0393.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui; on the road he took ill and died—age forty-seven.
s0393.idiomatic: When Chen perished he entered Sui; on the road he took ill and died at forty-seven.

s0394.literal: His son Junzhi was quite well known.
s0394.idiomatic: His son Junzhi was quite well known.

s0395.literal: Ruan Zhuo was a man of Weishi in Chenliu.
s0395.idiomatic: Ruan Zhuo was from Weishi in Chenliu.

s0396.literal: His grandfather Quan was a Liang regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
s0396.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan was a Liang regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

s0397.literal: His father Wendao was a Liang recorder of the staff in the Pacify-the-Far Prince of Yueyang's household.
s0397.idiomatic: His father Wendao was a Liang recorder of the staff in the pacify-the-far prince of Yueyang's household.

s0398.literal: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted in aim to the classics, skilled in discourse, and especially expert in five-character poetry.
s0398.idiomatic: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted in aim to the classics, skilled in discourse, and especially expert in five-character poetry.

s0399.literal: His nature was utmost filial; his father followed the Prince of Yueyang out to garrison Jiangzhou, met illness, and died—Zhuo was then fifteen and rushed from the capital to attend him, for many days taking neither water nor gruel.
s0399.idiomatic: His nature was utmost filial; his father followed the prince of Yueyang out to garrison Jiangzhou, met illness, and died—Zhuo was then fifteen and rushed from the capital to attend him, for many days taking neither water nor gruel.

s0400.literal: As Hou Jing's rebellion came, the roads were cut off; Zhuo braved danger and hardship and carried the coffin back to the capital.
s0400.idiomatic: As Hou Jing's rebellion came, the roads were cut off; Zhuo braved danger and hardship and carried the coffin back to the capital.
